Re: Internal appeal of denial for total shoulder replacement

Procedure: CPT 23472  
Reference number: POC-1EC0B0CD1F-92337  
Date of denial notice: August 10, 2026

Dear Molina Healthcare Appeals Department:

I am requesting an internal appeal of the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472. The denial states that the imaging findings submitted did not support medical necessity. The clinical record directly addresses that concern and demonstrates advanced structural disease, persistent symptoms, substantial functional impairment, and failure of appropriate nonsurgical treatment.

The imaging is significant. Shoulder radiographs obtained on June 5, 2026, using true AP and axillary views, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT imaging confirms that the rotator cuff is intact. These findings document severe glenohumeral joint destruction and provide objective support for the requested total shoulder replacement.

The patient has also had progressive symptoms for 24 months, including pain that has not been relieved by rest. The condition substantially limits daily activities. The patient cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without assistance, and cannot sleep on the affected side. Examination shows glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees. Cuff strength remains intact.

Appropriate conservative treatment has been attempted without adequate or durable relief. The patient completed 16 supervised physical-therapy visits over 12 weeks, from April 27, 2026, through July 20, 2026, with treatment focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening. The patient also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on June 17, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief. The physical-therapy discharge note documents completion of the supervised therapy course.

The patient does not have identified factors that would otherwise explain why the requested procedure should be denied. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. The patient is a nonsmoker, has a BMI of 29, and has intact cuff strength. The treating orthopedic surgeon, Okafor, MD, has requested the procedure based on the patient’s symptoms, examination, failed conservative treatment, and imaging findings.

I ask Molina to overturn the denial and approve CPT 23472. Please have the request reviewed by an orthopedic specialist or other physician with appropriate expertise in shoulder arthroplasty.

The specific Molina policy and clinical-review criteria applied to this denial have not been provided to me, and I have not located a publicly available Molina policy containing the applicable criteria for CPT 23472. Accordingly, this appeal does not quote or assume any Molina policy language. If Molina continues to uphold the denial, please provide the exact policy or clinical-review criteria used, including the policy number, version or effective date, the specific imaging requirements applied, the complete clinical rationale, and the qualifications of the reviewing clinician.

Please consider the enclosed records:

1. June 5, 2026, shoulder radiographs and report  
2. CT imaging and report confirming an intact rotator cuff  
3. Physical examination findings  
4. Physical-therapy records and discharge note documenting 16 visits from April 27, 2026, through July 20, 2026  
5. Medication history documenting six months of NSAID treatment  
6. June 17, 2026, corticosteroid-injection record documenting only two weeks of partial relief  
7. Orthopedic surgical recommendation from Okafor, MD  
8. The denial notice

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and issue a written determination. The appeal is being submitted within 180 days of the August 10, 2026, denial notice and no later than February 6, 2027.

Sincerely,

Riley Novak
